audit.why: HARD 8/10 is right for an immobile mage against an assassin with a 575-range leap and a free terrain vault. Win rate 51.85% over 2303 games says the lane survives the early game more often than the difficulty implies, which the text already handles by making the banked root the win condition.

Spike ladder matches the kits: Talon's level 6 Shadow Assault is 100/80/60s, his lane pressure comes from Rake dropping 9s to 7s and Noxian Diplomacy 8s to 6s, and Lux's counter-spikes are Final Spark (60/50/40s) and Luden's.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated that Lucent Singularity reveals stealth, which is the single most useful interaction Lux has against Shadow Assault. breakdown.cooldowns also carried no number. spikes[2].text credited Talon's wall-hop to his PASSIVE — it is Assassin's Path (E).
audit.why: Lux's E carries revealsStealth. Shadow Assault makes Talon Invisible until the blades converge, so dropping the E zone where he vanished both reveals and slows him. Blade's End is the bleed passive (3 Wound stacks); Assassin's Path is the free-cost, 725-range terrain vault whose cooldown is on the WALL, not the spell.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and breakdown.mid now name the E reveal; spikes[2].text now credits Assassin's Path (E) and explains the per-wall cooldown; cooldowns now carries 9s/7s Rake, 8s Q and 100s R.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Rake as "matchup-defining" without a single cooldown value (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Rake is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at 650 range and the returning blades are the damage half, so the punish window is concrete and short.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and 7s maxed; the returning blades carry most of his lane damage, so stand off the return line and step up while it is down. - Noxian Diplomacy is 8s and leaps from 575 out. - Shadow Assault is 100s at rank 1 and turns him invisible — your E reveals it.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Assassin's Path has no cooldown, only the terrain does — a centred wave and warded side walls remove the vault angles he opens on.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Holding Lucent Singularity for a bigger hit leaves you inside Rake's return line at half HP — detonate early and step out.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Talon wins by chipping with Rake, stacking Blade's End to three, then leaping Noxian Diplomacy in to burst the bleed.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by holding one root for his leap: Noxian Diplomacy comes from 575, so root at 1175 and Final Spark him before Rake returns.

edits.before: Luden's onward, every root is a kill: shove, hover the river, and Q-R the first contest. Your range decides objective setups alone.
edits.after: Luden's onward, hold E as a detector: Lucent Singularity reveals stealth, so the zone you drop where Shadow Assault ended is the pick.

edits.before: At 6 his ult (Shadow Assault) plus roam threat is lethal; he can all-in you or leave lane to snowball other lanes. Ward both sides, keep your Q (Light Binding) as a self-peel, and never facecheck when his ult is up.
edits.after: At 6 his ult (Shadow Assault) plus roam threat is lethal, but it turns him Invisible and Lucent Singularity reveals stealth — drop the E where he vanished, hold Q as self-peel, and ward both sides.

edits.before: One item and Talon's W-Q-passive combo deletes you before your combo lands. He also uses wall-hops from his passive to roam and dodge ganks. Farm safely, push to deny roam timing, and call for jungle when he vanishes.
edits.after: One item and Talon's W-Q-passive combo deletes you before your combo lands. He vaults walls with Assassin's Path (E), not his passive — it is free, but each wall he uses goes on a long cooldown. Push to deny his roam timing.
